extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political theory, historians, and commentators on American constitutionalism
extracted.subtask_short: analyzing durability of American republican institutions
extracted.subtask_description: A political-philosophical analysis of the causes that strengthen or threaten the United States Union and the permanence of republican institutions, identifying social, economic, communicative, and institutional factors that promote cohesion or disunion. The text offers criteria for judging when the federal system will hold or decay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosperity as a source of danger to the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosperity of the United States is the source of the most serious dangers that threaten them, since it tends to create in some of the confederate States that over-excitement which accompanies a rapid increase of fortune; and to awaken in others those feelings of envy, mistrust, and regret which usually attend upon the loss of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid and unequal increases in wealth produce social passions (envy, mistrust) that endanger the maintenance of the Union; examples include differing economic trajectories of Southern planters and Northern states, and commodity price changes (e.g., tobacco depreciation) that diminish some regions' opulence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population growth and national expansion as a cause of ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Americans of the United States must inevitably become one of the greatest nations in the world; their offset will cover almost the whole of North America; the continent which they inhabit is their dominion, and it cannot escape them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid demographic growth and the prospect of territorial expansion create incentives (riches, power, renown) that may spur rushing to seize national destiny — a factor that can exacerbate interstate rivalry or external ambitions affecting cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union depends on continued assent of all confederates
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence of the present confederation depends entirely on the continued assent of all the confederates; the Union may perish either because one State chooses to retire from the compact (secession) or because the Federal Government is progressively stripped of authority by tacit consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate Union durability by whether constituent states continually assent to federal authority and whether the central government retains sufficient prerogatives to perform its purpose; both abrupt secession and gradual erosion of federal power are failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and intermixing promote national unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The post, steamboats, inland navigation and other facilities of nature and art bring Americans into contact, causing them to intermingle, grow in resemblance, and diminish differences resulting from climate, origin, and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improved physical and intellectual intercourse (mail, transport, migration) fosters acquaintance and shared habits, accelerating assimilation toward a common national character and strengthening the Union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Migration and cultural assimilation fuse provincial characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Every year, thousands of men leave the North to settle in different parts of the Union: they bring with them their faith, their opinions, and their manners; ... This continual emigration of the North to the South is peculiarly favorable to the fusion of all the different provincial characters into one national character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the extent and directional bias of internal migration and the cultural influence of migrants; where a dominant regional civilization diffuses broadly, it becomes the common standard and aids national assimilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal power tends to decline after a crisis is resolved
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Constitution of 1789 was promulgated, the nation ... was a prey to anarchy; the Union reached a maximum of authority because it satisfied an imperious want. But once danger passed, the energy and patriotism which had enabled them to brave it disappeared; when a powerful Government no longer appeared necessary, they once more began to think it irksome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong central government that emerges to meet an emergency will often see its authority wane as prosperity and order return; judges of durability should watch for institutional retrenchment driven by public preference for lighter central intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political leaders and parties exploit anti-centralist tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders of parties, who live by the passions of the people, began to work [the tendency to limit federal power] to their own advantage. The position of the Federal Government then became exceedingly critical. Its enemies were in possession of the popular favor; and they obtained the right of conducting its policy by pledging themselves to lessen its influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how partisan incentives and demagogues channel popular antipathy toward centralization into concrete policy or constitutional constraints; party-driven curbs on federal authority can accelerate institutional weakening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy conflicts (internal improvements, Indian treaties, land sales, banks, tariffs) test and shape federal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific controversies—such as internal improvements, treatment of Indian tribes, sale and revenue from public lands, the Bank of the United States, and tariff policy—have repeatedly provoked claims of state sovereignty and produced concessions that reduced central authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outcomes of major intergovernmental policy disputes as indicators: concessions to states (or federal retreats) signal erosion of federal prerogatives; conversely, successful assertion of national control strengthens Union authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullification doctrine undermines constitutional union
rubrics_metrics.description: The partisans of Nullification ... maintain that each State retains its entire sovereignty ... and has the right of putting its own construction upon the laws of Congress, and of suspending their execution within the limits of its own territory ... A similar doctrine destroys the very basis of the Federal Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess threats to Union legitimacy by the prevalence of doctrines asserting unilateral state veto over federal law; widespread acceptance of such doctrines is a clear metric of constitutional breakdown risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternating federal strength: strong in war, weak in peace
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union is to subsist, but to subsist as a shadow; it is to be strong in certain cases, and weak in all others; in time of warfare, it is to be able to concentrate all the forces of the nation ... and in time of peace its existence is to be scarcely perceptible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure federal durability by its capacity to perform essential national functions in peace as well as war; a government limited to wartime mobilization but ineffective in peacetime governance indicates gradual loss of substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republican institutions rest upon manners, morality, religion, and respect for rights
rubrics_metrics.description: What is called the republic in the United States, is the tranquil rule of the majority ... The republicans in the United States set a high value upon morality, respect religious belief, and acknowledge the existence of rights. They profess to think that a people ought to be moral, religious, and temperate, in proportion as it is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the endurance of republican government by the depth of societal commitments to moral conduct, religious observance (as a social restraint), respect for vested rights, and general temperance; these social conditions form a resilient foundation that laws alone cannot replace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Majority power constrained by principles of humanity, justice, reason, and vested rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of the majority is not of itself unlimited. In the moral world humanity, justice, and reason enjoy an undisputed supremacy; in the political world vested rights are treated with no less deference. The majority recognizes these two barriers; and if it now and then overstep them, it is because, like individuals, it has passions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging political stability, test whether constitutional and social norms effectively restrain majoritarian impulses; the presence of widely respected moral and legal barriers mitigates tyranny of the majority and strengthens the republic.
